svg.text: One rule, two guards: the same Zod schema in the browser and in the backend
Concept 8 · the browser checks for convenience (fast, per field) · the backend checks again for security
One source, one copy, one checker
rule-basics.ts the rule's shape; it only
copies; don't change them here (change the
backend first, then copy them again)
login.ts: not a copy (the Login form)
CRLF (Windows) counts as the same as LF; one
changed character → DIFF … from line N, exit 1
The journey of one form input
Guard 1 · the browser: fast, per field
schema from the copied rule-basics.ts; Zod's built-in texts → friendly ones
off_above must be greater than on_below (hysteresis)
wrong input → no POST at all (lab: 0 requests); the focus
moves to the wrong field; this message = the backend's 400 text
the backend's guard: admin only, from a known page
+ a cron check with node-cron (not possible in a browser)
passes → saved in the rules table → 201 (create) or
200 (edit); the rule-changed event to every dashboard
rules read from the database are checked by this schema
too; unknown shapes are skipped with a WARN
back to /rules with the toast Rule "Water if soil < 30 %" saved.
the message is split per field → setError: "invalid cron expression" shows under the cron field;
an error for a field without a message place: "Refused by the server: …" above the Save rule button
• the backend's rules.ts imports node-cron, which
in the browser fileURLToPath is not a function,
the page never runs (a white screen)
• the frontend must build on its own, without
• the price of a copy: two places → the cure is
npm run check-schema + a PR template item
